subject: FinBank: private-network routing decision + allowlist items
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@finbank.com>
Cc: Netops Team <netops@finbank.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: recap & ask — FinBank Private network options

Hi Alice / NetOps team,

Thanks for the productive call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can converge on a deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC / PrivateLink):

- Preference we heard: compliance-first approach, leaning toward PrivateLink if it meets your routing/evidence needs.
- Hosted API: fastest to ship but does not provide fixed egress IPs (not ideal if you require strict allowlists).
- Dedicated capacity: we can reserve pools for you and provide more predictable egress addresses and isolation.
- Private VPC (customer-managed): gives you full network control (peering or PrivateLink), and you manage egress/egress IPs.

To move the network qualification forward, can you please confirm the following before our technical deep-dive?
1) Which connectivity model do you prefer to evaluate first (PrivateLink or VPC peering)? If undecided — confirm whether strict egress allowlist (only specific IPv4/IPv6 ranges) is a hard requirement.
2) For the allowlist: share the firewall template (CSV or CIDR list) of inbound CIDRs you will accept and any port restrictions. We typically need 443 for production traffic; management ports (22/3389) only if you want us to reach your resources.
3) Are you operating in a cloud region (AWS/Azure/GCP) that requires region-specific endpoints? Which region(s)?
4) TLS/SNI expectations: do you require mutual TLS (mTLS) or standard TLS with SNI?

Proposed next step: schedule a 60-minute network deep-dive with your NetOps + our infra engineer to walk the PrivateLink flow and the Dedicated egress matrix. I’m proposing Tue July 27 at 10:00am PT — does that work?

Attaching a short network checklist to help your team gather items in advance (stub attached).

Thanks — I’ll prepare an egress matrix for Hosted vs Dedicated vs PrivateLink so we can show what fixed IPs (if any) we can commit.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: redwood-network-checklist.pdf (stub)
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@finbank.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Netops Team <netops@finbank.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: recap & ask — FinBank Private network options

Thanks, Olga — good summary. A couple of clarifications from NetOps so we can scope the work: 

Hi team, Alice from FinBank NetOps here. A few concrete items: 
- We strongly prefer PrivateLink from a compliance standpoint (no inbound peering across our VPC boundary). That said, we need explicit egress/ingress IPs to be allowed on our outbound firewall and on-prem perimeter.
- Please send the expected outbound IP ranges for: Hosted (if any), Dedicated, and any AWS endpoints that PrivateLink would expose. We block all outbound traffic except an explicit allowlist — so we need CIDR(s).
- Ports: production traffic will be over 443. Management plane questions: will you need SSH or remote management? If so, we need exact source IPs.
- TLS: we terminate TLS on our side; we do not currently support mTLS for third-party endpoints. Confirm whether Redwood needs mTLS for PrivateLink.
- Region: we operate primarily in us-west-2 and us-east-1. If you require a regional endpoint we need to know which region to provision.

I attached a simple allowlist-template.csv — please populate the columns with expected CIDRs and a note describing the purpose.

Can you also confirm whether Dedicated gives us static egress IP(s) we can include in our firewall? If Dedicated is the path, we may need a short procurement note to justify the commit.

Thanks — happy to schedule the deep dive. Tue July 27 10am PT works for the network team.

—Alice
Alice Turner
Principal Network Engineer, FinBank
alice.turner@finbank.com
NetOps Team: netops@finbank.com

Attachment: allowlist-template.csv (stub)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 19:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: recap & ask — FinBank Private network options

Quick internal note before the deep-dive:
- Hosted API: no guaranteed static egress IPs — we rely on shared egress pools; not recommended if customer requires firewall allowlist enforcement.
- Dedicated: we can allocate NAT egress ranges and provide a small set of static IPs per dedicated cluster/region (we'll produce the egress matrix).
- Private VPC / PrivateLink: customer-managed. For PrivateLink we expose an endpoint service backed by our NLB/ALB — the endpoint IPs come from the customer's VPC (AWS PrivateLink) but we can provide the endpoint DNS and required SG/route guidance. If they want explicit IPs, Dedicated is easier; otherwise PrivateLink avoids direct peering.

Action items I will own before the call:
1) Produce a short egress matrix CSV: Hosted / Dedicated / PrivateLink — what, if any, IPs we can commit per region.
2) Draft a short procurement note describing the difference and trade-offs (latency, security, operational overhead).
3) Add an infra engineer (I'll loop Maria Chen from infra) to the deep-dive invite.

Olga — I can have the egress matrix over to you by EOD tomorrow so you can pre-populate their allowlist template.

Thanks,
Rishi
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@finbank.com>
Cc: Netops Team <netops@finbank.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: recap & ask — FinBank Private network options

Great — thanks Alice and Rishi. Confirming next steps and logistics: 

- Deep-dive confirmed: Tue Jul 27, 10:00am PT — invite to follow with dial-in and an infra attendee (Maria).
- Rishi will send the egress matrix by EOD Wed (tomorrow) so you can complete the allowlist-template.
- Please complete the allowlist-template.csv with any CIDRs you accept and return it before the call if possible — will speed the decision.
- For the call we will cover: PrivateLink flow (DNS, SGs, endpoint lifecycle), Dedicated egress guarantee (NAT/static IPs), and the procurement implications of reserved capacity.

Attaching the updated checklist and a simple diagram showing PrivateLink vs peering options (stubs).

If FinBank prefers, we can run a short pilot in Dedicated (2-week) to validate performance and provide static egress while you finalize procurement.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
